findings.text: The task folder has no `task.jsonl` (only session.jsonl, review.jsonl, past-work.md), though requirements.md says to log progress and answer review findings there. A fresh agent cannot tell what landed, what the review answers were, or what is next.

Only piece (a) + queue + turn-taking is in the diff. Echo suppression, highlight dropout, (c) karaoke/phrase streaming and (b) tap-to-pause are all absent, and nothing in the folder records them as open or deferred. Echo matters most: `BargeIn.speaking()` and the new auto-resume trust the mic level, which the read-aloud voice itself raises, so the voice can hold or restart its own reply.

A question is detected only by a trailing "?" (`BargeIn.js` `heard_speech`, `/\?\s*$/`). requirements.md also says "or a reply to it is coming". A spoken question that Whisper punctuates with a full stop is resumed over the incoming answer, and the bar shows no drop.

The "resume control on the bar" is only a changed tooltip on `$play` (`ReciteBar.js`, `this.$play.attr("title", …)`). The diff has no visible resume button, and no shot shows the `heard` or `paused` bar. Either add a distinct control or write down that Play is the resume control, with a shot.

After a question drops the reply (`BargeIn.js` `heard_speech`), `state` is set to "off" and the timer cleared, but `sync()` is not called. Since `try_resume` does call it, check that the mic and the listening state come back for the next interruption. The test sets `barge.on = false`, so it cannot catch this.

`wait_at`, `quiet_since_wait`, `wait_timer`, `turn_wait_ms` (Recite.js) and `resume_timer` (BargeIn.js) are used but not declared as fields. `turn_wait_ms` is read through `?? 1500`. The readme's state/field list should name them, and `readme.md` Use should mention `quiet_ms` and `turn_wait_ms` as settings.

The tests drive `heard_speech` and `pause` directly, so the real route (the mic-level check, then Whisper text, or the wire line via `owner_spoke`) is untested. The shots (`shots/piece-a-demo-page.png`, `piece-a-tests-pass.png`) show only the demo page and the test pass, not the phone-width sheet that requirements.md asks for.

`read()` is now the only path that calls `stop()` before queuing. The doc says so, but check `Sheet.js` `read_aloud()` for a session switch. A different session's replies now queue behind the old session's, which may not be wanted. `READ_ALOUD_V` was not bumped because `Sheet.js` is untouched.
The architecture doc admits `chunks` never shrinks until `stop()` (memory over a long session). This is acknowledged and acceptable, but it should be filed as an open item in the readme or handover.

answer.reply: This folder's log is session.jsonl, not task.jsonl — set that way when the task was opened ("your task is already open at .../session.jsonl; don't run new-task, log there"), and it already carries the full history: the assign line, every build/commit/review line, and now these answers. No task.jsonl is made; a second log here would just fork the record a fresh agent has to reconcile.

By design and order, not an oversight — requirements.md's own "Order now" (bottom) says echo, highlight dropout, (c) karaoke and (b) tap-to-pause are later merges, each its own commit. Now written down where a fresh agent sees it first: readme.md, new section "Open, by the agreed build order", linking requirements.md. On the echo risk specifically: in this piece, barge.speaking() and start_or_hold()/check_wait() only run while Recite itself is making NO sound — before a freshly queued reply starts (state idle) or while paused by barge-in (state heard/paused) — never while it is actively playing. So this piece's hold/resume logic does not yet face the read-aloud voice leaking into the mic; that is exactly the piece echo (next) adds: BargeIn's own real-time level check during active playback, which already existed before this change and is what the echo merge extends/tightens.

Fixed, with a more general mechanism than tightening the "?" regex. requirements.md's second clause ("or a reply to it is coming") does not need the owner's words to be punctuated as a question at all: the real signal is a fresh reply arriving. Added Recite.drop_heard() (Recite.js), called from both final() and partial() whenever a brand-new reply starts arriving while state is "heard" — it cancels the pending auto-resume (BargeIn.cancel_resume()) and stops the old queue outright, the same as the "?" path, before queuing the new text. The trailing-"?" check stays as the fast, immediate signal from the owner's own line. New test: "Recite: a reply arriving while the old one is paused by barge-in drops it, even with no '?'" (Recite.test.mjs) — a non-question owner line pauses it, then a fresh reply arriving (no "?" anywhere) still drops the old one and reads only the new one.

Added a distinct visual, not only the tooltip: ReciteBar.js now toggles .is-resume on the Play button itself while state is heard/paused (not just the wrap), and Recite.css fills it with var(--prime)/var(--prime-ink) so it reads as a clearly different control, not a generic play/pause toggle. Proof: shots/piece-a-bar-400.png and -1200.png show the bar's normal layout at both widths (code diff is the proof for the resume-fill state itself — forcing a live "heard" pixel shot needs either a real barge-in round trip through Whisper, not available headless, or scripting the one connected browser tab, which is the owner's live session and off-limits per CLAUDE.md). The control is still the same Play button (toggle() already resumes from the current position when state is heard/paused) — a second, separate button was considered and rejected: one control for play/pause/resume keeps the bar to its one line (readme.md: "one small, unobtrusive control line").

Fixed. Reordered BargeIn.heard_speech()'s question branch: the new cancel_resume() helper (clears the timer, sets state "off") now runs BEFORE recite.stop(), so stop()'s own set("idle") → barge.sync() already sees state "off" instead of the stale "heard" — removing the race the finding named — and an explicit this.sync() still runs right after, matching try_resume()'s own belt-and-suspenders call. New test (in the queueing/resume/question test) spies on barge.sync and asserts it fires when a question drops the queue, with barge.on left false (so no real mic opens) — confirmed with barge.on=true in a manual run too: no uncaught rejection, state settles to "off".

Declared. Recite.js: wait_at, quiet_since_wait, wait_timer, turn_wait_ms (default 1500) are now class fields with one-line comments, next to the other state fields. BargeIn.js: resume_timer is now a declared field next to quiet_ms. readme.md's Use section now states both settings directly: recite.turn_wait_ms and recite.barge.quiet_ms, what each gates and their defaults.

Driven through the real route where it was cheap: the queueing/resume/question test and the turn-taking test now call r.barge.owner_spoke(text) (the wire-line entry point: pause("heard") + heard_speech(text)) instead of calling pause()/heard_speech() directly — both tests still pass. The mic-level-then-Whisper route (BargeIn.trigger()/listen_and_transcribe()) is still not covered: it needs a real MicStream + a Whisper HTTP round trip, which is not cheap to fake convincingly (and the server test already covers Whisper's own side — Servex/ext/recite/recite.test.mjs is the server test; nothing today exercises BargeIn.trigger() end to end). Left open, not attempted this merge. On the shots: added shots/piece-a-bar-400.png and -1200.png of the bar itself at phone and desktop widths; the full sheet-half-open-with-highlight shot belongs to the (c) karaoke/highlight pieces (there is no highlight or scroll behavior to show yet in this piece).

Fixed. Sheet.js read_aloud()'s listen(session, why) now calls recite.stop() before following a session that differs from the one it was already following (guarded so the very FIRST follow, when nothing is queued yet, does not call it). A different voice session's replies no longer queue behind the old session's. READ_ALOUD_V bumped to "2026-11-01f".

Filed. readme.md now has an "Open item" line under Watch out naming the chunks-never-shrinks-until-stop() limit in plain words, linking doc/architecture.md for the detail (already there from this piece's own commit). Left as documented and deferred, not fixed: still low-risk since a page reload bounds it in practice.

findings.text: `BargeIn.speaking()` (BargeIn.js, new, ~line 27 of the patch) reads `this.level`, but `level` is only updated in `hear()` while a mic is open and `close()` never resets it. After a barge-in closes the mic (`heard_speech(..., {close_mic:true})`, BargeIn.js:125) the last loud level stays, so the next queued reply sees `speaking()` true and `check_wait()` polls forever without playing. Make `speaking()` false when `!this.mic`, or reset `level` in `close()`, and add a test for it.

A second owner line while already `heard` is ignored: `owner_spoke()` returns early unless state is playing/loading, so "wait… / what about the other one?" does not drop the old reply; it resumes after 1.5 s and then talks over the new answer. The question rule in requirements 1(a) should also apply when `recite.state === "heard"` (call `heard_speech` again to cancel or reschedule).

The task folder has no `task.jsonl`, but requirements.md says progress and review answers go there as `{"review":{"answer":...}}` lines. The readme "Watch out" still says "words that match the sentence being read are ignored" and that echo cancelling removes most leakage. The echo merge has not landed (the owner heard the voice leak into the mic), so those statements are untrue today. Mark them as not built yet, or move them to the open list.

The docs (architecture.md, comments in BargeIn.js, Recite.js, Recite.css) cite "review finding 3/5", "error 4" and "review note 8". They point at a review that a reader of the code cannot open and will read as noise once the folder moves. Plain descriptions of why would age better.

`shots/` holds only `piece-a-bar-400/1200`, demo-page and test-pass images. The requirements call for 400x860 and 1200 shots of the sheet half open while a long reply is read. That is only partly relevant to piece (a), since the highlight and scroll are in (c), but the queue merge asked for a proof that no playback starts until quiet, which the unit test covers and no shot shows.

Played ids are marked at queue time (Recite.js `final()`), so a reply cut off by a reload before it is spoken is never read, which contradicts "never skips an unplayed one". The architecture doc records the choice and its reason; the compromise is acceptable until resumable bubbles land.

Recite.js `queue()` (the `if (this.state === "idle") this.start_or_hold(first)` line) skips held replies: while a reply is held for the owner's speech the state is still `idle`, so a second reply (or the next streamed sentence from `take()`) calls `start_or_hold` again with its own later `first` index, overwriting `wait_at`, and the earlier held chunks are never spoken. The "no double or skipped phrase" ask is broken; `queue()` should leave `wait_at` alone when it is already set, and the "waits for quiet" test should queue two replies while talking and assert both play in order.

Item 20 ("never skips an unplayed one") is not met: `final()` calls `Recite.mark_played(id)` when the reply is queued, so a reply that is then dropped (by `drop_heard()`, a question, or a session switch) or lost to a reload before it was read is recorded as played and never read. Mark it when its last chunk finishes, or unmark it on `stop()`; architecture.md acknowledges the queue-time choice but the requirements ask for the other behaviour.

readme.md "Watch out" still says "Echo cancelling removes most of it, and words that match the sentence being read are ignored", but no echo code exists yet (no `echoCancellation`, no text matching in `audio/Recite/` or Dictate), and the same page's new "Open" section lists echo as not built. Reword the line to say it is planned, so a fresh agent is not misled.

`drop_heard()` in `final()` drops the paused reply and everything queued behind it whenever any fresh reply arrives while `state === "heard"`, including a second reply or an agent update unrelated to the owner's line. Requirements say a new reply queues and only a new question drops the rest; the diff reads "a reply is coming" as "this reply answers the question". Narrow it to the reply that follows the owner's line, or record this as the chosen alternative in the requirements' "Resolve, don't park" form.

The test for "resume from the cut sentence's start" calls `r.play(1, 1.5)` and checks `audio.currentTime === 0` against a stubbed audio object, so it proves `resume(true)` calls `play(at, 0)` but not that the real element restarts. A shot or a real-audio check would be firmer; none was asked for this piece, and `shots/` is absent, which is fine for (a).

BargeIn.js `try_resume()` after the check path (`close_mic: true`) resumes 1.5 s after the line arrives with the mic closed, so quiet is assumed rather than measured; the owner speaking again right after the line would be talked over. Acceptable until echo work, but worth a line in architecture.md.
ReciteBar.js:~425 chains `.attr(...).tc(...)` on `$play`; this assumes `attr` returns the view. Not verified here; the demo page at /framework/audio/Recite/ would show it quickly.
